sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Henderson County?
sections.html:
Henderson County splits the work between the Assessor, who sets values, and the Tax Collector, who bills and collects. Both are in the county office building at 200 North Grove Street, Hendersonville, NC 28792, and the Tax Collector's office is Suite 66 on the ground floor, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 5:00.

Questions about an appraisal or appeal go to 828-697-4667, and payment questions go to 828-697-5595. The Assessor does not set tax rates. The Board of Commissioners and the governing bodies of Hendersonville, Fletcher, Saluda, Mills River, Flat Rock and Laurel Park each set their own to meet their budgets.

The Tax Collector bills for the county, thirteen fire districts, the City of Hendersonville, the Town of Laurel Park and the part of Saluda that lies in Henderson County. The Assessor's page counts 22 tax districts, including the general county district, and rates vary with the services each district provides.

sections.h2: How does Henderson County value property?
sections.html:
The Assessor must value everything taxable at 100% of market value, using the uniform standards in G.S. 105-283. The office handles about 71,500 parcels, roughly 4,500 businesses with business personal property, more than 10,000 manufactured homes and more than 100,000 registered vehicles billed monthly.

Henderson County reappraises every four years rather than waiting for the eight-year state limit in G.S. 105-286. The last reappraisal was in 2023, and the next takes effect January 1, 2027. Buildings still under construction on January 1 are valued by their percent complete, and a farm or forest tract in the Present-Use Value Program is assessed below market.

Property tax supplies an estimated 50% of the county's total operating budget in fiscal year 2027, according to the county's reappraisal page.

sections.h2: What is the Henderson County 2027 reappraisal schedule?
sections.html:
The county's published schedule runs from the Schedule of Values hearing in fall 2026 through tax bills in August 2027. Notices of assessed value are expected to go out around February 1, 2027, so owners will see new numbers before the appeal window closes.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Henderson County assessment?
sections.html:
Put an informal appeal in writing to the Assessor first, using the county's standard form, and take a formal appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review only if that does not settle the value. The formal appeal must arrive before the board's adjournment date.

  • After a formal appeal is filed, an appraiser meets with the owner to discuss the value and check the owner's information.
  • If the owner and appraiser still disagree, both sides present at a public hearing.
  • The board's decision is mailed within 30 days of the hearing.
  • A further appeal to the state Property Tax Commission must be filed within 30 days of the board's notice, and most of those cases are heard in Raleigh.

The general state process is in G.S. 105-322. For a seller, the strongest evidence is recent sales of similar homes nearby, an appraisal from the sale contract, and repair quotes for defects the mass appraisal could not see.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Henderson County tax bill?
sections.html:
Payment is by mail, in person, online, or through an automated phone system. In person, the office accepts cash, check, money order and cards, and a drop box in the south parking lot is checked daily, though cash should not go in it.

  • Card and e-check payments carry a convenience fee paid to the payment vendor, not to the county.
  • Prepayments are accepted from January through July and show as a credit on the bill.
  • Owners who cannot pay on time are told to call before the bill becomes delinquent, and most can arrange a payment plan.
  • Mail checks to Henderson County Tax Collector, 200 N Grove St, Ste 66, Hendersonville, NC 28792.

State law makes taxes due September 1 and payable at face value through the day before January 6, then adds 2% interest and three-quarters of one percent monthly, as laid out in G.S. 105-360.

sections.h2: What relief programs are open to Henderson County homeowners?
sections.html:
With 29.1% of residents 65 or over, the age-based programs reach many owners. The county's tax pages list the elderly or permanently disabled exclusion, the disabled veterans exclusion, present-use value and the circuit-breaker deferral, all filed with the Assessor.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or half the appraised value of the permanent residence, with a 2026 income limit of $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income cap.
  • Circuit breaker: tax held to 4.0% of income, or 5.0% when income is above $38,800 and up to $58,200, with the excess deferred.

A single owner can use only one of those three, and the application is Form AV-9, accepted through June 1 before the tax year. A circuit-breaker deferral becomes due on a transfer.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Henderson County tax, and what does it mean for a sale?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector may foreclose on real property with delinquent taxes, and sales are held on the courthouse steps at 200 North Grove Street. The county lists each parcel with an estimated opening bid that does not include interest and expenses accruing daily. Upset bid amounts are available from the Clerk of Court at 828-694-4100, and sale questions go to 828-698-3090.

The sale posted on the county page was May 27, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. and listed 15 parcels with estimated opening bids from $739.08 up to $14,077.24.

An owner with a balance who wants to sell instead can pay it from proceeds at closing. Ask the Tax Collector for the payoff, and expect the deed excise tax of $1.00 per $500 to be paid separately by the seller. For context on the market, the Census Bureau lists a median owner-occupied value of $351,400, 75.0% owner occupancy, median household income of $68,187 and 1,093 building permits in 2025 (Census QuickFacts).

faqs.q: When is the Henderson County reappraisal effective?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027. The county's last reappraisal was in 2023 and it follows a four-year cycle, so values reset to market as of that date.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Henderson County 2027 value?
faqs.a: The county schedule shows the Board of Equalization and Review adjourning and closing the 2027 appeal period on May 14, 2027. Informal appeals to the Assessor run from January 1 to April 13, 2027.

faqs.q: Can I pay Henderson County property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. The Tax Collector encourages monthly installments, accepts prepayments from January through July, and usually offers a payment plan if you call before the bill is delinquent.

faqs.q: Where are Henderson County tax foreclosure sales held?
faqs.a: On the courthouse steps at 200 North Grove Street, Hendersonville. The Tax Collector's page lists each parcel and an estimated opening bid, and the Clerk of Court gives current upset bid amounts.

faqs.q: Who sets the Henderson County tax rate?
faqs.a: The Board of Commissioners sets the county rate, and each municipality sets its own. The Assessor only determines value, so an appeal changes the value and not the rate.
